newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs edge up, Caribs continue to climb.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs edge up, Caribs continue to climb.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier rates were slightly firmer on Tuesday after a heavy load of fixtures on Monday, brokers said.
Fixtures included the 290,000 tonne Tartar which was set to sail from the Iraqi port of Mina al-Bakr to the U.S. Gulf at W55 for Bayoil, loading April 10.
VLCC fixtures eastwards, especially to South Korea, were more numerous, however, with the rate for 250,000 tonnes to Singapore firming to W67.5 from W62.5/65, brokers said.

"Six or seven ships were fixed yesterday Middle East/east. Rates are moving up even though today hasn't been as busy. Next week could see an improvement to around W70 for a modern ship," one broker said.

The U.S./upcoast sector continued its spectacular climb of recent weeks, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes hitting W250, against a 1996 average of W148 and a February average of just W131.6, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc.
U.S./upcoast 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged up to W215 from W212.5.
The West Africa market was quieter, with brokers quoting W70 for a 260,000 tonne VLCC to the U.S. and W97.5 for a 130,000 tonner.
In the Mediterranean, 130,000 tonne cargoes were unchanged at around W100 in quiet trade, with 80,000 tonnes also flat at W120. Inter-U.K./cont 80,000 tonne vessels remained at a firm W140.
Fuel oil firmed five points to W205 for 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont and to W210 cross-Med. "There's simply no tonnage for prompt dates on the Continent," an Italian broker said.
